facts.text: Eagle Crater was deployed at Meridiani Planum during Opportunity (MER-B) in 2004.

Opportunity landed inside Eagle Crater, a small 22-metre impact crater. Scientists called it a 'hole in one'. The crater walls exposed layered bedrock containing tiny haematite spherules nicknamed 'blueberries'. This was the first in-situ evidence that liquid water once existed on the Martian surface.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Exposed layered bedrock and haematite spherules that provided the first in-situ proof of ancient liquid water on the Martian surface.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Meridiani Planum.
Eagle Crater is where Opportunity made its 'hole in one' landing; the exposed bedrock remains a landmark site in the history of Mars exploration.
